props.title: Come and See
props.initialSlug: A boy faces war's nightmarish horror in WW2 Belarus

sections.content: **Come and See** (1985) stands as arguably the most devastating anti-war film ever made. Director Elem Klimov's unflinching portrayal of Nazi atrocities in Belarus follows 14-year-old Flyora through increasingly nightmarish scenarios, using innovative sound design and closeup photography that puts viewers inside his traumatized perspective. The film's influence echoes through later war films like **Saving Private Ryan** (1998) and **The Painted Bird** (2019), though few dare to match its raw intensity. Klimov's use of hypnotic tracking shots and surreal imagery creates a hallucinatory effect that makes the horror feel inescapably real.

sections.content: The film's technical innovations remain groundbreaking. Klimov used live ammunition during battle scenes and employed a special camera rig called the Steadicam Arm to achieve the film's signature floating perspective. The lead actor Aleksei Kravchenko's face was captured aging in real-time through the traumatic shoot, creating an unprecedented document of war's psychological toll. This influenced later works like **Lebanon** (2009) and **Son of Saul** (2015), which similarly use intimate camera work to convey war's immediate horror.

The film's unflinching depiction of civilian casualties and village burnings draws direct parallels to real Wehrmacht atrocities in Belarus, where over 600 villages were destroyed. This documentary-like approach influenced films like **Downfall** (2004) and **Anthropoid** (2016), though **Come and See** remains unique in showing the Holocaust from a child's perspective, making its impact all the more devastating. sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond just Eastern European cinema. Its dreamlike atmosphere and psychological horror elements can be seen in films like **Apocalypse Now** (1979) and **The Thin Red Line** (1998). Contemporary directors like Christopher Nolan have cited its innovative sound design, where subjective hearing loss and tinnitus put viewers inside Flyora's traumatized headspace. This technique influenced works like **Dunkirk** (2017) and **1917** (2019).
